title: Consolidated quarter sprint backlog for hosted endpoints and model maintenance
creator: Asha Ramesh
description:
Goal: Create a single, prioritized sprint backlog and execution playbook that aligns Hosted API endpoint work and model-catalog maintenance to Q2 OKRs. This ticket bundles scope, acceptance criteria, rollout sequencing, and telemetry gating for model rotations, deprecation windows, and canary schedules so engineering, infra, and docs teams can execute with minimal ad-hoc coordination.

Background: Over the last three quarters we've had duplicate planning artifacts for hosted endpoints and model catalog changes. That has led to missed canaries, unclear rollback criteria, and inconsistent cost/latency measurement across similar model swaps. This work consolidates decision points, defines evaluation gates, and instruments dashboards to support safe, repeatable rotations.

Scope (deliverables):
- Single sprint backlog (CSV + Linear view) that merges endpoint config changes, model onboarding/deprecation tasks, eval suites, and rollout ops steps.
- Playbook doc with step-by-step canary plan (traffic slices, duration, metrics, rollback thresholds).
- Canonical gating checklist for model acceptance: perf (latency, p95), cost delta, quality regression threshold on core prompt set, and infra readiness.
- Telemetry dashboards and alerts: model-health, per-route latency/cost, and prompt-set regression trend.
- RBAC checklist for who can approve canaries and final rollouts.
- Post-rollout template for regression monitoring and cost reconciliation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sprint backlog created and prioritized by PM + ENG lead with explicit owner for each task.
- Playbook published in Confluence with sign-off from Reliability, Research/Applied ML, and Platform Security.
- Canary automation scripts or runbooks exist for the top 3 hosted endpoints (chat, generate, embed).
- Dashboards show baseline and canary windows; alerts trigger when regression thresholds exceeded.

Design & trade-offs:
- Trade-off: faster rotation cadence (bi-weekly) increases ops overhead and risk. We propose a conservative cadence of monthly roster rotations for major models but allow smaller minor-quantization updates on a bi-weekly opt-in schedule. This balances customer impact and ops cost.
- Trade-off: strict quality thresholds reduce rollouts but increase time to market for cheaper backfill models. We adopt asymmetric thresholds: stricter for high-traffic endpoints, looser for low-traffic/experimental endpoints.

Runbook highlights:
1) Pre-canary checklist: eval suite pass (quality), perf benchmark (p50/p95 within target), cost delta under configured threshold, infra capacity verified, data retention & privacy checks.
2) Canary step: 1% traffic -> monitor 6 hours; 5% -> monitor 12 hours; 20% -> 24 hours; full. At each step enforce automated rollback if p95 latency increases >20% or quality drop >3% on critical prompt set.
3) Post-rollout: 7-day regression monitoring window and cost reconciliation report to Finance.

Telemetry & dashboards:
- Temporary dashboard scope: route-level token-cost, p50/p95/p99 latency, model-inference-error-rate, and eval-score-delta for the canonical prompt set. Links: Confluence playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Consolidated+Quarter+Sprint+Backlog ; Roadmap artifact GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/roadmaps/pull/123 ; Canary runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/playbooks/pull/78 ; Dashboard (staging): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/model-health?q=quarterly-backlog

Stakeholders & approvals required:
- AP (Product Ops): sign-off on schedule and OKR mapping.
- Reliability Eng: approval on canary thresholds and automation.
- Applied ML: quality gating and test-suite ownership.
- Security & Compliance: ensure no new model introduces data handling risks.
- Finance: cost target alignment for the quarter.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Unexpected downstream latency spikes due to quantized variants. Mitigation: enforce perf test harness on dedicated hardware before canary.
- Risk: Evaluation blind spots for niche prompts. Mitigation: expand core prompt set with top 50 customer utterances per route; add smoke tests.
- Risk: Insufficient observability for multi-tenant billing. Mitigation: instrument token-level cost attribution for canary windows.

- 2026-03-11 (Priya S): Completed perf harness run for quantized v1; results flagged a 12% p95 regression on A100. Decision: require optimization pass (ENG-1842) before canary.
- 2026-03-12 (Lena P): Draft Confluence playbook published for review: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Consolidated+Quarter+Sprint+Backlog . Requested signoffs from Reliability and Security.
- 2026-03-14 (Asha R): Consolidated feedback from Reliability; canary thresholds tightened for high-traffic routes. Added dependency on ENG-33210 and ENG-1842.

Open questions:
- Do we require Finance approval for every major model swap that increases per-token cost by >10%? (Proposal: yes, for high-traffic endpoints only).
- Should we automate canary rollback via orchestration or require human-in-loop for the 5%->20% transition? (Proposal: automated for low-risk metric-only failures; human-in-loop for quality regressions).
